hero.title: Build the card sorter
hero.description: Parts list and assembly instructions for the physical sorting unit: a hopper feeds cards one at a time through {{modules}} stacked routing modules, each capable of dropping a card into one of two side bins or passing it down to the next module - {{bins}} bins total, driven by an {{arduino}} over I²C.
hero.modulesIntro: Each module has three servos - a <0>bottom</0> trapdoor, a <1>paddle</1> gate, and a left/right <2>pusher</2> - plus an IR sensor. Closing every trapdoor above the target bin and opening only the ones beneath it lets a card fall to the right module before the pusher ejects it.

bom.heading: Bill of materials
bom.description: Quantities scale with the number of modules you're building - {{modules}} modules × 3 servos, 1 feeder, {{irSensors}} IR sensors, {{channelsUsed}} of the PCA9685's 16 channels in use. The remaining channels are free for additional sorting modules (up to 5 modules on a single PCA9685). Check off each part as you gather it - checkmarks are saved in this browser.

arduino.notes: Runs {{path}}; USB connection to the host computer for Web Serial

pca9685.notes: I²C servo driver - drives all 10 servos

sg90Positional.notes: 3 per module × {{count}} modules - bottom trapdoor, paddle gate, pusher

sg90Continuous.part: SG90 servo, modified for continuous rotation
sg90Continuous.notes: Feeder - drives cards out of the hopper into module 1

irSensor.notes: One at the gate of each module (1-{{count}}), plus one in the hopper throat

psu.notes: Dedicated servo bus power into the PCA9685 V+ terminal - do not power 10 servos off the Arduino's onboard 5V

usbCable.notes: Arduino Uno R4 Minima ↔ host computer

barrelJack.part: DC barrel jack or screw-terminal pigtail
barrelJack.notes: Adapts the PSU output to the PCA9685's V+ / GND terminal

enclosure.notes: Print from <mesh>card_sorter.3mf</mesh> (mesh, slicer-ready) or <source>Card Sorter.f3d</source> (Fusion 360 source)

filament.notes: Quantity per your slicer's estimate for the model above

oRing.notes: Fitted onto the feeder roller for grip on the card face

m3x6Screw.notes: 14 attach each bin base to the housing; 8 attach the base panels to the base

m3Nut.notes: Paired with the base panel M3×6 screws

m2x4Screw.notes: 11 per module ({{count}} modules): flapper (bottom/sides), pusher arms, and IR sensor mounts

m2x6Screw.notes: Mounts the Arduino and PCA9685 servo driver board to the base panels

servoHornScrew.notes: Included with each servo; secures the horn to the shaft

hookupWire.notes: IR sensor/Servos. Using these you may have to daisy chain some together, just electrical tape them to make sure they don't come apart.

dupontConnectors.notes: These are only needed if you're making your own custom length wires.

dupontCrimper.notes: These are only needed if you're making your own custom length wires.

wiring.heading: Wiring
wiring.description: Everything hangs off one I²C bus (PCA9685) and {{count}} digital input pins (IR sensors). The PCA9685's logic side runs off the Arduino's 5V; its <pin>V+</pin> servo rail must come from the external supply, and that supply's ground must be tied back to the Arduino's ground - a floating servo ground is the most common reason a freshly wired unit won't move.

diagram.title: Wiring diagram
diagram.alt: Wiring diagram showing the PCA9685, Arduino, servo, and IR sensor connections

irSensors.description: All {{count}} read active-LOW (pin goes low when a card is present) using the Arduino's internal pull-up - wire the sensor's digital OUT straight to the pin, no external pull-up resistor needed.

channelMap.unused: Unused - available for additional sorting modules

assembly.heading: Assembly
assembly.description: Eight phases, structural work first. Checkboxes are saved in this browser, so you can close the tab mid-build and pick back up later.
assembly.helpText: Stuck on a step? Join the Discord if you need help.

printEnclosure.text: Slice and print the enclosure and three module housings from <mesh>card_sorter.3mf</mesh> (or re-export from <source>Card Sorter.f3d</source>).
printEnclosure.note: PLA is fine for the housings; PETG if the unit will sit somewhere warm.

printSupportPieces.text: For {{modules}} sorting modules, print {{count}} generic base support pieces from the same file - the modules stack in a staircase, so each added tier needs one more support piece than the tier above it. Change the module count in the parts list above to update this.

printBasePlates.text: For {{modules}} sorting modules, print {{count}} additional generic base plates - the standard build (3 modules) doesn't need any extra; print one more base plate for each sorting module beyond the initial 3. Change the module count in the parts list above to update this.

dryFit.text: Dry-fit each module housing before inserting any electronics - sand or adjust any tight servo pockets now.

mountBoardsToPanels.text: Mount the Arduino and PCA9685 servo driver board to the base panels with 8 M2×6 screws.

attachBasePanels.text: Attach the base panels to the base with 8 M3×6 screws and 8 M3 nuts.
attachBasePanels.note: Do this after the Arduino and PCA9685 are mounted to the panels - the boards are much harder to reach once the panels are on the base.

installLibraries.text: In the Arduino IDE, install the ArduinoJson and Adafruit PWM Servo Driver libraries.
installLibraries.note: Library Manager → search each by name.

uploadSketch.text: Select board "Arduino Uno R4 Minima", select the correct port, then upload arduino/main/main.ino.

confirmReady.text: Open the Serial Monitor at 9600 baud and confirm you see {"status":"ready"} after the board resets.

mountModuleServos.text: Install the bottom, paddle, and pusher servo into each of the 3 module housings (9 servos total).
mountModuleServos.note: Center each servo at its neutral pulse before screwing down the horn, so mechanical range matches the firmware's open/closed travel.

mountBottomFlapper.text: Attach the bottom flapper to the bottom servo's horn with M2×4 screws, servo held at its closed pulse so the flapper seats flush across the card path.
mountBottomFlapper.note: This is the trapdoor a card falls through to reach the next module, or the current one on a match.

mountSideFlappers.text: Before attaching anything, command each paddle servo through its full range to confirm the linkage can reach fully open without binding. Then, with the servo held at its closed position, attach the left and right flapper to the shared linkage with M2×4 screws (one pair per module) so both sit flush and even.
mountSideFlappers.note: One paddle servo drives both flappers together - they open and close as a pair, not independently. Fit the flappers closed first; the exact open-position pulse gets fine-tuned later from the Module Calibration Grid.

mountPusherArm.text: Before fitting the arm, sweep the pusher servo through its full left-to-right range and find its true mechanical middle. With the servo held at that middle position, attach the card pusher arm to the horn with M2×4 screws so it sits centered between the left and right bins.
mountPusherArm.note: Fitting the arm off-center biases the push distance to one side - the exact left/right pulses get fine-tuned later from the Module Calibration Grid.

fitFeederOrings.text: Fit 6 G20 o-rings onto the feeder roller.
fitFeederOrings.note: These give the roller grip on the card face - space them evenly along the roller's length.

mountFeederRoller.text: Attach the roller to the feeder module.

mountFeederServo.text: Install the continuous-rotation feeder servo to the roller, at the base of the hopper.

mountFeederWall.text: Attach the wall piece to the tube that guides cards from the hopper to the feeder roller.
mountFeederWall.note: When mounting the wall, attach it to the feeder module first, then put 2 cards below the wall and slide it down before tighting it into place.

mountModuleIr.text: Fix one IR sensor at the gate of each module (1-{{modules}}), aimed across the card path.

mountHopperIr.text: Fix the remaining IR sensor in the hopper throat, just above the feeder.
mountHopperIr.note: This one tells the feeder when the hopper is empty - placement matters more than the module sensors.

wireI2c.text: Wire the PCA9685 to the Arduino's I²C bus (SDA/SCL) and 5V/GND for logic power.

wireServos.text: Wire all 10 servos into PCA9685 channels 0–8 and 15 per the channel map - the feeder always takes the last channel.
wireServos.note: There are wire channels, that use zip ties, in the side of the base to help keep everything neat.

wireSensors.text: Wire the {{count}} IR sensors to the digital pins listed in the Wiring section above - module gates and the hopper throat sensor don't all fall on consecutive pins.
wireSensors.note: For the power and ground, you will have to combine {{count}} wires into one, either with a breadboard or by twisting and soldering them together. You will need to manually calibrate the sensors to have a shorter throw, as to not get false positives.

wirePower.text: Bring the external 5V supply into the PCA9685 V+/GND terminal, and tie its ground to the Arduino's ground.
wirePower.note: Skipping the common ground is the #1 cause of servos that twitch but never move correctly.

runTestCommand.text: With the external servo supply connected, send {"test": true} over serial.
runTestCommand.note: Cycles every bottom and paddle open, sweeps all pushers left then right, resets to neutral, then briefly spins the feeder.

watchModules.text: Watch each module during the test - confirm nothing binds or grinds at the end of its travel.
watchModules.note: If a servo strains at open or closed, its housing cutout likely needs adjusting before calibration.

connectSerial.text: Connect the Arduino to the app via Web Serial, then open /app/calibrate.

calibrateModules.text: Module Calibration Grid - set the open/closed pulse for each bottom and paddle, and left/neutral/right for each pusher, module by module.

calibrateFeeder.text: Feeder Calibration Panel - tune feed speed, pulse/pause timing, and settle duration against your actual hopper.

checkIr.text: IR Sensor Panel - verify all {{count}} sensors report present/absent correctly with a card in hand.

testBins.text: Bin Routing Controls - send a test card to each of the 7 bins in turn and confirm it lands correctly.

loadHopper.text: Load the hopper and confirm the feeder stops pulsing once the hopper IR reads empty.

fullPass.text: Run a full scan-to-bin pass end to end before leaving the unit unattended.
